volume.tooltip: Speaker level (−∞…0 dB). 0 dB is unity. Default −3 dB. Old patches that stored 0…1 linear Volume are converted on load. Type a dB value (or −inf).

pan.tooltip: Stereo balance after Mono is summed in. 0 = unchanged (Mono to both). −1 = left only. +1 = right only.

segments.tooltip: How many wedges the picture is folded into around the centre. A whole number: modulated, it steps from one count to the next.

angle.tooltip: Turns the wedge, in degrees: which part of the picture is folded. -180 to 180 is half a turn either way.

mirror.tooltip: Mirror reflects every other wedge, the classic kaleidoscope. Rotate repeats the same wedge around the centre. No glide; modulated, it switches at the halfway point.

centerX.tooltip: Horizontal position of the centre the picture is folded around. -1 left edge, 1 right edge.

centerY.tooltip: Vertical position of the centre. -1 bottom, 1 top.

input.tooltip: How much of the incoming picture is added each frame. 0 lets the feedback run on its own.

decay.tooltip: How much of the previous frame is kept each frame. 1 never fades, 0 keeps nothing (no feedback).

zoom.tooltip: How much the previous frame is scaled each frame, in percent: positive pulls it outward, negative sucks it in. It happens once per frame, so the pattern it makes does not depend on frame timing.

rotate.tooltip: How far the previous frame is turned each frame, in degrees, and which way. Once per frame, so a turn that is a simple fraction of the wedge angle makes patterns that hold still and walk. Fine around 0.

shiftX.tooltip: How far the previous frame slides sideways each frame, in percent of the picture.

shiftY.tooltip: How far the previous frame slides up or down each frame, in percent of the picture.

blend.tooltip: How the new picture meets the faded previous one. Screen never clips hard (the default). Add stacks light and clips. Max keeps the brighter of the two, so trails never build up. Over lays the new picture on top, more where it is bright. No glide; modulated, it steps through the four.

hue.tooltip: How far the colours of the previous frame turn around the colour wheel each frame, in degrees, and which way. The colour shift builds as the picture feeds back, so trails cycle through the spectrum. Once per frame. Fine around 0.

blur.tooltip: How much the previous frame is softened each frame, so detail diffuses into glow as it feeds back. 0 is off.

srcX.tooltip: Slides which part of the incoming picture the wedge looks at, sideways.

srcY.tooltip: Slides which part of the incoming picture the wedge looks at, up or down.

srcZoom.tooltip: How much of the incoming picture the wedge sees: above 1 zooms in on a smaller part, below 1 shows more of it.

saturation.tooltip: How much the colours are pushed toward intense each frame, and it compounds as the picture feeds back: turned up, even muted colours build into vivid ones. Negative drains the colour away. Fine around 0.

punch.tooltip: A contrast curve on the fed-back picture: dim, muddy mixes fade faster while bright cores stay, so the colour stays vivid instead of washing toward white. 0 is off.

jitter.tooltip: How far the picture's scanlines land left or right of where they should. Neighbouring lines move together, so it reads as one unsteady signal. 0 is off.

roughness.tooltip: How much each line goes its own way. 0 is a smooth drift across the lines, 1 is every line independent, a torn picture.

jitterRate.tooltip: How fast the jitter moves. 0 to 1 runs from slow (0.1x) to 6x; past 1 it keeps climbing, +6x for every unit, up to 6000x. At very high rates the motion is faster than the frame rate can show, so it aliases into slow, structured patterns.

wobble.tooltip: A slow sideways sway down the picture, like a weak horizontal hold. 0 is off.

wobbleRate.tooltip: How fast the sway moves. 0 to 1 runs from slow (0.1x) to 6x; past 1 it keeps climbing, +6x for every unit, up to 6000x. At very high rates it aliases into slow, structured stripes.

ringing.tooltip: Faint echoes trailing to the right of sharp edges, as an overworked cable rings. 0 is off.

ringX.tooltip: Horizontal direction and spacing of the ringing echoes. 1 trails them to the right of an edge, -1 to the left.

ringY.tooltip: Vertical direction and spacing of the ringing echoes. 1 trails them above an edge, -1 below. With X and Y at 0 there is no ringing.

bleed.tooltip: Smears the picture sideways, as a limited bandwidth does: sharp vertical edges soften. 0 is off.

noise.tooltip: A light static grain over the picture. 0 is off. (Streaky static, dropouts and glitches are in the Analog Glitch module.)

instability.tooltip: How much the speeds and amounts wander on their own, slowly and without repeating, so the signal is never a steady loop. 0 is perfectly steady.

hum.tooltip: How dark the hum bars are. 0 is clear, 1 is black.

humBars.tooltip: How many bars cross the picture at once.

humWidth.tooltip: How wide each bar is, from a thin line to a broad band.

humSpeed.tooltip: How fast the bars travel, in half-screens per second, and which way: positive rolls up, negative down. Fine around 0, where it creeps as a real hum does against the frame rate. Far from 0 it aliases against the frame rate into slow, structured bars.

wiggle.tooltip: A sideways ripple in the picture where a bar passes, whether or not the bars are dark. 0 is off.

wiggleRate.tooltip: How fast the ripple moves. 0 to 1 runs from slow (0.1x) to 6x; past 1 it keeps climbing, +6x for every unit, up to 6000x.

magnet.tooltip: The strength of a magnet held to the screen at the XY pad's position: it bulges or pinches the picture there, swirls it and stains its colours. 0 is off.

magX.tooltip: Horizontal position of the magnet. -1 left edge, 1 right edge.

magY.tooltip: Vertical position of the magnet. -1 bottom, 1 top.

magPull.tooltip: Whether the magnet bulges the picture out (positive) or pinches it in (negative).

magSwirl.tooltip: How much the picture twists around the magnet, and which way.

magSize.tooltip: How far the magnet's field reaches.

magPurity.tooltip: How much the magnet pulls the red, green and blue apart, staining the colours around it the way a real magnet does to a tube.

instability.tooltip: How much the hum speed, the wiggle and the magnet's strength and position wander on their own, slowly and without repeating, so the distortion is never a steady loop. 0 is perfectly steady.

mode.tooltip: RGB: Ch1 red, Ch2 green, Ch3 blue. CMY: Ch1 cyan, Ch2 magenta, Ch3 yellow. No glide; modulated, it switches at the halfway point.

blend.tooltip: Additive sums phosphor light (default). Over composites the plates in order. No custom blend formula. Modulated, it switches at the halfway point.

hue.tooltip: Turns the source's colours around the colour wheel before the split, in degrees. ±360° is one full turn either way.

range.tooltip: How far the three XY pads reach. 1 is the full reach (±12% of the face). Lower it for a subtle fringe: it falls off steeply, so 0.2 reaches about 0.5% and 0.1 about 0.1%.

ch1X.tooltip: Ch1 horizontal shift. ±1 is 12% of the face. Positive moves right.

ch1Y.tooltip: Ch1 vertical shift. ±1 is 12% of the face. Positive moves up.

ch1Bright.tooltip: Ch1 plate level. 0 is off, 1 is full. Read once per simulation frame.

ch1Blur.tooltip: Ch1 Gaussian radius. 0 is one texel. 1 is about 6 pixels.

ch2X.tooltip: Ch2 horizontal shift. ±1 is 12% of the face. Positive moves right.

ch2Y.tooltip: Ch2 vertical shift. ±1 is 12% of the face. Positive moves up.

ch2Bright.tooltip: Ch2 plate level. 0 is off, 1 is full. Read once per simulation frame.

ch2Blur.tooltip: Ch2 Gaussian radius. 0 is one texel. 1 is about 6 pixels.

ch3X.tooltip: Ch3 horizontal shift. ±1 is 12% of the face. Positive moves right.

ch3Y.tooltip: Ch3 vertical shift. ±1 is 12% of the face. Positive moves up.

ch3Bright.tooltip: Ch3 plate level. 0 is off, 1 is full. Read once per simulation frame.

ch3Blur.tooltip: Ch3 Gaussian radius. 0 is one texel. 1 is about 6 pixels.

width.tooltip: Horizontal bow. 0 is flat. Positive bows the sides outward, like a CRT. Negative bows them inward.

height.tooltip: Vertical bow. 0 is flat. Positive bows the top and bottom outward. Negative bows them inward.

round.tooltip: Squircle screen edge. 0 is a sharp rectangle, around 0.7 a squircle, 1 an ellipse.

vignette.tooltip: Darkens the picture toward the edges of the glass. 0 is off, 1 goes all the way to black at the glass edge.

vigReach.tooltip: How far in from the edge the darkening starts. 0 hugs the corners, 1 darkens from the center.

vigCurve.tooltip: How sudden the vignette falls. 0 is a long soft gradient, 1 is a hard shadow edge. With Vignette at 1 the outside goes fully black.

vigShape.tooltip: The outline the vignette follows. 0 is an oval. 1 is the shape of the glass edge (see Roundness), so the dark follows the screen outline and, with Vignette at 1, reaches pure black exactly at the glass edge: no screen edge, just a soft shadow.

glareX.tooltip: Horizontal position of the glare. -1 left edge, 1 right edge.

glareY.tooltip: Vertical position of the glare. -1 bottom, 1 top.

glare.tooltip: A soft reflection on the glass and a faint sheen along its rim. 0 is off.

glareSize.tooltip: How big the glare spot is. 0 a small hot spot, 1 a broad wash.

shadowAlpha.tooltip: A shadow hugging the glass edge, like the enclosure casting onto the screen. How dark it gets at the edge. 0 is off, 1 is black. It follows the glass outline (Roundness).

shadowThick.tooltip: How far in from the glass edge the rim shadow reaches. It falls off softly into the picture.

pitch.tooltip: Picture rows per scanline, a whole number so the lines sit on the pixel grid and never beat against it. 2 is the finest. Modulated, it steps from one whole number to the next.

depth.tooltip: How dark the gaps between the lines are. 0 is no lines, 1 is the full raster. Past 1 it is over-applied: the gaps clip to black and the middle of each line is pushed brighter than the picture.

beam.tooltip: How much the beam widens where the picture is bright, so bright areas fill the gaps and dim ones show them. 0 keeps every line the same width. Past 1 it is over-applied: even dim areas widen, so the lines fill in everywhere except the darkest parts and bright areas bloom past their own line.

red.tooltip: The red channel's gain. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes it, 2 doubles it.

green.tooltip: The green channel's gain. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes it, 2 doubles it.

blue.tooltip: The blue channel's gain. 1 leaves it alone, 0 removes it, 2 doubles it.

hue.tooltip: Turns every colour around the colour wheel, in degrees. ±180° is half a turn either way.

saturation.tooltip: How intense the colours are. 0 leaves them, -1 drains them to grey, 1 triples the colour.

lightness.tooltip: Brightness. Positive lifts the picture toward white, negative darkens it toward black.

contrast.tooltip: Positive pushes lights and darks apart around the middle grey, negative squeezes them together.

gamma.tooltip: The brightness of the midtones, with black and white held where they are. Below 1 darkens them, above 1 lifts them.

tintHue.tooltip: The colour of the tint: a position on the colour wheel, in degrees (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue).

tint.tooltip: How much the picture is washed with the tint colour. 0 is off.

invert.tooltip: Turns the picture into its negative. 0 is off, 1 is fully inverted, 0.5 is flat grey.

drift.tooltip: The hue wanders around the wheel on its own, at this speed and in this direction. 0 is still. It keeps going, so it never repeats the same colours twice in step with anything else.

spread.tooltip: The hue changes across the picture instead of being the same everywhere: a rainbow gradient from one corner to the other. 0 is off.

threshold.tooltip: How bright a part of the picture has to be before it blooms. Lower lets more of the picture glow.

bloom.tooltip: How strongly the bright parts bleed light into their surroundings. 0 is off, 1 is full, above 1 is over-driven.

glow.tooltip: A broad, soft haze over the whole picture, built from the bloom. 0 is off.

dim.tooltip: Darkens the picture itself, so the bloom and glow stand out against it. 0 is off, 1 is black.
